Store the sufficient statistics of one analysis

Source: R/infra-class.R
new_sufficient_stats.Rd

The central object of the share direction. Users get one from sufficient_stats(); new_sufficient_stats() is the low-level constructor. The check functions do not use it: they work from reported numbers.

Usage

new_sufficient_stats(
  handler,
  verdict,
  verdict_reason,
  stats = list(),
  meta = list(),
  disclosure = list(),
  lost
)

is_sufficient_stats(x)

Arguments

handler

Name of the registered handler that made the object.

verdict

One of verdicts().

verdict_reason

Why this verdict, in one sentence.

stats

Named list of sufficient statistics, stored at full precision (means, covariance matrix, counts, per-cluster summaries, ...).

meta

Named list of metadata: complete-case n, contrasts, effect_size_conventions, rounding, ss_type.

disclosure

Named list of disclosure flags (small cells, small clusters, extreme values). A risk reduction, never a guarantee.

lost

Required: character vector of what readers lose compared with the raw data.

x

An object.

Value

An object of class reprokit_sufficient_stats.

Details

Authors never call this constructor: sufficient_stats() builds the object and fills lost from the test.

This constructor cannot make an object without a non-empty list of what readers lose. The author's reason for not sharing is not stored here: it belongs to appendix() alone, is optional, and is never filled in by reprokit.

Examples

s <- new_sufficient_stats(
  handler = "example",
  verdict = "summaries_suffice",
  verdict_reason = "Group means and SDs determine the t statistic.",
  stats = list(n = c(20, 22), mean = c(5.1, 4.3), sd = c(1.2, 1.4)),
  lost = c("outlier inspection", "alternative analyses")
)
s
#> <reprokit sufficient_stats>  analysis: not recognised
#> Verdict: summaries_suffice
#> Because: Group means and SDs determine the t statistic.
#> To publish: NA (appendix() writes this out).
#> What readers lose compared with the raw data:
#>   * outlier inspection
#>   * alternative analyses
#> Statistics stored: n, mean, sd
